stories.title: Myanmar human rights conditions hit new low, says UN
stories.summary: Human rights in Myanmar have worsened, with widespread abuses against the Rohingya by both the military and Arakan Army, including killings, torture, and forced displacement. The military-influenced election secured junta chief Min Aung Hlaing’s presidency amid ongoing violence causing over 8,075 civilian deaths and 3.6 million internally displaced people. Illegal rare-earth mining has expanded rapidly, funding conflict and causing severe environmental pollution affecting local communities and neighbouring countries like Thailand. Human rights conditions in Myanmar have sunk to a new low, with widespread abuses against the Rohingya minority and a booming illicit economy driven partly by illegal rare-earth mining deepening civilian suffering, the United Nations said on Aug 25. The UN Human Rights Office report, covering June 2025 to May 2026, said unrelenting conflict, military violence and a growing “conflict economy” were exposing civilians to severe hardship. Both Myanmar’s military and the Arakan Army, which controls much of western Rakhine state, had committed widespread, systematic violations against Rohingya communities, including killings, torture, forced recruitment, forced labour, arbitrary detention and displacement. Neither responded to a Reuters request for comment. Nine years after the 2017 exodus that forced hundreds of thousands of Rohingya to flee, and following further abuses since the 2021 coup that ousted the democratically elected government of Nobel Peace Prize winner Aung San Suu Kyi, the community remains subject to systematic discrimination, the UN said. The military engineered an election earlier in 2026 that allowed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing to become president. The military has continued relying on air strikes, arson and aid restrictions to impose fear and maintain control more than five years after the coup, killing at least 8,075 civilians since 2021, including 1,774 women and 1,074 children – a toll the UN said is likely far higher. The Myanmar military has previously said it conducted limited air strikes on military targets in response to violent seizures of towns and villages by insurgents and what it describes as terrorist groups. Internal displacement had risen to 3.6 million people, the UN said, while 12.4 million face acute hunger and some 400,000 mothers and children suffer acute malnutrition.

stories.title: Will Iran withdraw from nuclear non-proliferation treaty?
stories.summary: Iranian lawmakers have again raised the possibility of leaving a decades-old international nuclear weapons treaty. Analysts say the threat to quit may offer Tehran more leverage than an actual withdrawal.

stories.title: Survivors of Guinea's deadly landfill collapse say authorities ignored warnings
stories.summary: Two days after a deadly landfill collapse in Guinea, rescuers are using giant excavators to search for victims. Anger is rising among residents, who say they had warned authorities that the rubbish dump was precarious.

stories.title: Russia, Vatican maintain trustworthy relations — Foreign Minister Lavrov
stories.summary: The top Russian diplomat said the sides welcomed the upcoming meeting between the Secretary of the Holy See and Metropolitan Anthony of Volokolamsk, head of the Moscow Patriarchate's Department for External Church Relations
article_sentences: Russia and the Vatican maintain trustworthy relations, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said after his meeting on Tuesday with Vatican Secretary for Relations with States Paul Richard Gallagher.
"I am glad to welcome my colleague back to Moscow.
The last time we met here was in November 2021.

We noted with satisfaction that, against the background of the fundamental changes in the geopolitical situation that have taken place during this period, relations between the Russian Federation and the Vatican remain trustworthy, friendly and pragmatic," Lavrov said at a joint press conference with Gallagher in Moscow.
"We welcome the upcoming meeting between the Secretary of the Holy See and Metropolitan Anthony of Volokolamsk, head of the Moscow Patriarchate's Department for External Church Relations.
It is intended to bring fresh momentum to the inter-church dialogue, which we support," Lavrov added.
